```{=typst}


#import "@preview/fletcher:0.5.8": diagram, node, edge

#diagram(
  node-stroke: 0.8pt,
  node-fill: rgb("f9f9f9"),
  spacing: (15mm, 10mm),

  // Inputs and weights
  node((0, 0), $x$, radius: 5mm),
  node((0, 1), $w_1$, radius: 5mm),
  node((0, 2.5), $w_2$, radius: 5mm),
  node((0, 3.5), $y$, radius: 5mm),

  // Multiplication
  node((1.5, 0.5), $times$, radius: 6mm, name: <mul1>),
  node((1.5, 3.0), $times$, radius: 6mm, name: <mul2>),

  edge((0, 0), <mul1>, "->"),
  edge((0, 1), <mul1>, "->"),
  edge((0, 2.5), <mul2>, "->"),
  edge((0, 3.5), <mul2>, "->"),

  // Addition
  node((3.0, 1.75), $+$, radius: 6mm, name: <add>),

  edge(<add>, <act>, "->", label: $z$, label-pos: 0.5, label-side: auto),
  edge(<mul2>, <add>, "->", label: $w_2 y$, label-pos: 0.4, label-side: right),

  // Activation
  node(
    (4.5, 1.75),
    $sigma$,
    radius: 6mm,
    fill: rgb("e6f2ff"),
    stroke: blue + 1pt,
    name: <act>,
  ),

  edge(<add>, <act>, "->", label: $z$, label-pos: 0.5, label-side: auto ),

  // Output
  node((6.0, 1.75), $f(x, y)$, stroke: none, fill: none, name: <out>),
  edge(<act>, <out>, "->"),
)
```

```{=typst}
#diagram({
  node((0, 0), [A], name: <A>)
  node((4, 0), [B], name: <B>)

  edge(<A>, <B>, "->", shift: 3pt)
  edge(<A>, <B>, "<-", shift: -3pt)
})
```

```{=typst}

node((2,0), $f$, stroke: blue, shape: rect),
)\
```

### Consider the function:

```{=typst}
$
f(x, y) = (x + y)y
$
```

::: {#fig-computation-graph}

```{dot}
digraph computation_graph {
  graph [
    rankdir = LR,
    bgcolor = "transparent",
    nodesep = 0.45,
    ranksep = 0.7
  ];

  node [
    shape = circle,
    style = filled,
    fillcolor = "#EAF2FF",
    color = "#3B6EA5",
    fontname = "Helvetica",
    fontsize = 10,
    margin = 0.08
  ];

  edge [
    color = "#4A5568",
    arrowsize = 0.75
  ];

  x   [label = "x"];
  y   [label = "y"];
  add [label = "+"];
  mul [label = "×"];
  f   [label = "f"];

  x -> add;
  y -> add;
  add -> mul;
  y -> mul;
  mul -> f;
}
```

A computational graph for the function above.

:::

The forward computation introduces an intermediate value:

```{=typst}
#import "@preview/diverential:0.3.0": *
$
u = x + y \
f = u y
$
```

For the reverse pass:

```{=typst}
$
dvp(f,u) = y \
dif f / dif x
  = (dif f / dif u)(dif u / dif x)
  = y
$
```

The variable \(y\) occurs along two paths, so its contributions add:

```{=typst}
$
dif f / dif y
  = underbrace(dif f / dif y)_(text("direct path"))
  + underbrace(
      (dif f / dif u)(dif u / dif y)
    )_(text("through ") u) \
  = u + y \
  = x + 2y
$
```
